notes: Both coders gave the one document the same stance (delegates, four tiers). Most disagreement was about type for borderline passages (e.g. P10 vs P66 for students' reluctance to ask, P51 vs P97 for accommodation referral, P39 vs P69/P53 for reasons against detectors, P04/P83 vs P35 for assessment-design items); I resolved by re-reading the passage and choosing the type a reader seeking that rule would expect, noting the partial fit. Modality differed on 'effective uses' list items (informs vs may): resolved to informs since the text grants no permission. Actor differed on the detector reasons (instructor vs all): resolved to instructor since the section addresses instructors. unit_stance differed where a unit concerns communication rather than AI use: set to neutral. Coder B found 15 units A missed (scope and software integration, summary scope, list items, CELT offerings, AI-literacy framework pointers); A found 10 B missed (hallucination statement, delegation clause, separate misuse items, assessment principles, list intros). All one-sided units were checked against the source and kept. Coders' topic vocabularies differed; the final file uses coder A's starter-codebook topics, and coder B-only units were mapped to starter codes. Matching used anchor overlap, with the CELT/Provost sentences matched by hand.
